title: Deception by Omission: Using Adversarial Missingness to Poison Causal Structure Learning

problem.claim: Causal structure learning from observational data must operate when training data may be incompletely observed, creating an attack surface for biased causal structure inference.

gap.claim: Existing adversarial perturbation attacks on completely observed data are invalidated when data correctness can be audited, such as through cryptographic signatures.

contributions.claim: Introduces an adversarial missingness attack that deceptively omits part of the true training data to bias learned causal structures.
Derives theoretically sound attack mechanisms for arbitrary structural causal models.
Provides a sample-efficient learning-based heuristic for adversarial missingness attacks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present adversarial missingness as a novel attack methodology.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real and synthetic data sets reportedly demonstrate the effectiveness of adversarial missingness attacks against popular causal structure learning algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causality-informed machine learning is positioned as useful for generalization, fairness, robustness, and interpretability.
Causal structure inference from observational data is identified as a key component, with incomplete observation arising in practice.
Prior attacks perturb completely observed training data, but auditable data correctness invalidates that mechanism.
The work proposes deceptive omission of true training samples to bias causal structure learning and develops general attack mechanisms plus a learning-based heuristic.
Real and synthetic data experiments reportedly show effectiveness against popular causal structure learning algorithms.

source_observation.claim: When training-data correctness is auditable, adversarial omission can remain an available route for manipulating causal structure learning.

interpretation.claim: Integrity validation of observed samples does not by itself establish integrity of dataset completeness.

application.claim: Security reviews of causal learning pipelines should consider missingness and dataset completeness as attack surfaces.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that adversarial missingness is the only available strategy outside the stated strong signed-sample validation model.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the attack mechanism details, assumptions, or guarantees.
The abstract does not identify the real and synthetic data sets or the evaluated algorithms.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, or computational costs.
